doc.name: A — headphones catalogue, hands in frame, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: over-ear studio headphones
Category: headphones
Shot programme: hands in frame
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this headphones product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the tilted dynamic in a hands in frame treatment.

SUBJECT. A over-ear studio headphones. Lock the product itself to the reference — no proportional drift, no invented branding, no cleaned-up typography. Everything else in the frame is your design decision.

CAMERA. Camera rolled into a deliberate tilt with the product on a diagonal. Shoot on a 40mm anamorphic at f/22, framing for deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with an overcast soft dome with no directional shadow at all. Stage the product on or against honed travertine, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a filmic grade with halation on the specular highlights. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
